text:
maria: overnight we saw ~6 OOMs across prod-inference-01/02 between 00:30-01:15 UTC. all tied to long-context chat sessions >18k tokens, KV cache grew unbounded and hit RSS ceiling. logs attached: kv_spill=true trace=tr-9a3c
chris: saw the same. flamegraph points to kv_insert hot path plus a big spike when kernel switched to the new fused-attn variant at 00:28. suspect kernel selection + reuse heuristics are interacting badly.
andre: repro locally with long-dialog harness. if we enable kv_reuse + aggressive prefetch and larger batch windows, memory jumps. repro script: `scripts/repro/longctx_kv_stress.sh --tokens 20000`
ci-bot: build #4021 finished, perf artifact: https://ci/redwood/4021/artifacts/kv-profiles.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
priya: profiling summary: majority allocations are small slab fragments + new shard allocations during page compaction. compaction is paused too late, causes fragmentation growth.
sophie: quick mitigation: throttle background compaction so it runs more often but with smaller work quanta (reduce peak). also limit concurrent shard rehydrates to 2. this reduces transient RSS spikes.
vikram: alternative fast-fix: clamp kv_cache_max_live_shards=512 (was 4096) and enable fallback to zero-copy paging. will do a canary.
maria: we need a graceful-degrade plan if throttle fails: 1) fallback to quantized small model (q4_0) on that route 2) disable kv_reuse for requests >15k tokens 3) automatic 429-with-retry-backoff if memory pressure detected.
andre: agree. also add a soft-reject policy: when kv:allocation_rate>threshold, return partial stream + header `x-kv-degraded: true`.
chris: note: batching heuristic also caused bursts — we batch up to 32 streams; when many long clients rejoin we create short-lived allocation spikes at batch boundaries. propose adaptive batch cap that shrinks when mean sequence>8k.
priya: attached small patch that does compaction throttling + early-eject for tiny fragments. snippet:
```
// reduce compaction quantum when mean_live_tokens > 8k
if (stats.mean_live_tokens > 8_000) compaction.quantum = max(64, compaction.quantum / 4);
```

vikram: rolling this as hotfix to prod-dedicated-1 at 05:00 UTC. patch will include kv_cache_max_live_shards clamp + compaction throttle. will monitor mem:kv_rss and evict_count metrics.
maria: add telemetry tag `kv_mitigation=compaction_throttle_v1` and trace IDs for any 5xx/oom. good to surface in console.
ci-bot: canary deploy to prod-dedicated-1 started (canary id c-778). monitoring hooks: dashboards updated.
priya: tests: added unit for early-eject and an integration that simulates concurrent long sessions for 60s. perf baseline before patch: peak rss 94GB, after patch: 68GB on same load.
sophie: also plan non-invasive behaviour: when we detect repeated OOMs within same host, autoscale fallback to smaller model and route new sessions to healthy hosts.
andre: let's ship. steps: 1) hotfix canary 2) observe 2 hours 3) progressive rollout 25/50/100 4) postmortem if failures.
maria: thanks all. follow-up: create an alert that fires when kv_fragmentation_ratio>0.6 and kv_evict_rate<0.1 with ops runbook linking to this thread. assigning runbook owner: @vikram. :eyes:
chris: noted. I'll open the PR with the kernel selection guard to avoid picking fused-attn for long-inflight sessions. :shipit:
